title: Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric

source.effective_note: The study guide gives no effective date for its skills list. The 19 October 2026 date in the Academy brief is unverified; this version is named for the page's own update date.

notes: The bullets illustrate how each skill is assessed; related topics may also be tested.
Most questions cover generally available features; commonly used Preview features may appear.
KratosForge readiness is an estimate from evidence on this PC, never Microsoft's score or a promise of passing.

domains.title: Implement and manage an analytics solution

objectives.competency: Choose and configure Spark pools, environments and Spark settings for a workspace's workloads.
Assign workspaces to domains and set the settings a domain can delegate.
Set a workspace's OneLake settings and know what each one allows.
Set the workspace settings for data workflows (Apache Airflow jobs) and know when they apply.
Connect a workspace to Git, commit, branch, update and resolve conflicts in item definitions.
Develop a warehouse as a database project and catch breaking changes before they deploy.
Create a deployment pipeline, set deployment rules, and know what deploys and what doesn't.
Give people the least workspace role that lets them do their work.
Share individual items with the permissions each audience needs.

objectives.text: Implement row-level, column-level, object-level, and file-level access controls
objectives.competency: Restrict rows, columns, objects and OneLake folders to the people allowed to see them.
Apply dynamic data masking and know who sees masked and unmasked values.
Apply sensitivity labels to items and know how labels flow to downstream items.
Promote and certify items and know who may do each.

objectives.text: Choose between a pipeline and a notebook
objectives.competency: Choose between a pipeline and a notebook for a job and justify the choice.

objectives.text: Design and implement schedules and event-based triggers
objectives.competency: Schedule pipelines and trigger them from events such as a file arriving.

objectives.text: Implement orchestration patterns with notebooks and pipelines, including parameters and dynamic expressions
objectives.competency: Orchestrate notebooks and pipelines with parameters and dynamic expressions.

objectives.text: Design and implement full and incremental data loads
objectives.competency: Build full and incremental loads that miss nothing and are safe to run again.

objectives.text: Prepare data for loading into a dimensional model
objectives.competency: Prepare dimensions and facts for a dimensional model, including surrogate keys and history.

objectives.text: Design and implement a loading pattern for streaming data
objectives.competency: Design a loading pattern for streaming data that resumes where it left off.
Choose a lakehouse, warehouse, eventhouse or SQL database for a workload.

objectives.text: Choose between dataflows, notebooks, and T-SQL for data transformation
objectives.competency: Choose dataflows, notebooks or T-SQL for a transformation and justify the choice.

objectives.text: Create and manage shortcuts to data
objectives.competency: Create and manage shortcuts to data in OneLake and outside it.
Set up mirroring and know what it replicates and how to query it.
Ingest data with pipeline activities, including copy settings that suit the source.

objectives.text: Transform data by using PySpark, SQL, and KQL
objectives.competency: Transform data with PySpark, SQL and KQL.
Denormalize data into wide tables for reporting.
Group and aggregate data, including subtotals.

objectives.text: Handle duplicate, missing, and late-arriving data
objectives.competency: Handle duplicate, missing and late-arriving data without losing or doubling rows.
Choose Eventstream, Spark structured streaming or KQL for a streaming workload.
Process events with an eventstream: filter, aggregate and route them.

objectives.text: Process data by using Spark structured streaming
objectives.competency: Process data with Spark structured streaming, including checkpoints and foreachBatch.
Process streaming data with KQL.
Aggregate events over tumbling, hopping, sliding and session windows.

domains.title: Monitor and optimize an analytics solution

objectives.competency: Monitor ingestion runs and find failures and slowdowns.
Monitor transformation runs and capacity use and find what caused a problem.
Monitor semantic model refreshes and spot problems such as Direct Lake fallback.
Configure alerts that fire on failures and on data conditions.
Find and fix pipeline errors.
Find and fix dataflow errors.
Find and fix notebook errors.
Find and fix eventhouse errors.
Find and fix eventstream errors.
Find and fix T-SQL errors.
Optimize lakehouse tables: file sizes, layout and maintenance.
Optimize a pipeline's run time and cost.
Optimize a data warehouse.
Optimize eventstreams and eventhouses.
Optimize Spark performance.
Optimize query performance.

gaps.title: No local KQL engine
gaps.why: Nothing in the repository runs KQL
gaps.closes_with: Fabric Eventhouse exercises (ACD-014), or embedding Microsoft's Kusto emulator if Chris approves installing it (ACD-016)

gaps.title: No Eventstream runtime
gaps.closes_with: Topology checks locally (SIMULATED), real runs in Fabric (ACD-014)

gaps.title: T-SQL never runs here
gaps.why: DuckDB is not the Warehouse engine (sql_dialects.py)

gaps.title: Workspace, tenant and domain settings, roles and endorsement
gaps.why: Settings and permissions live in Fabric; some need admin roles
gaps.closes_with: SIMULATED settings models locally, read-only checks in the learner's own workspace

gaps.title: Sensitivity labels
gaps.why: Needs sensitivity labels published in the tenant
gaps.closes_with: FABRIC VERIFIED only where the learner's tenant has labels; otherwise KO

gaps.title: Mirroring
gaps.why: Needs a source database and capacity
gaps.closes_with: KO locally; Fabric exercise with a free-tier source is a cost decision for Chris

gaps.title: Data workflows (Apache Airflow jobs)
gaps.why: No local Airflow job runtime in KratosForge

gaps.title: Spark engine and continuous streaming
gaps.why: The local PySpark API is DuckDB: no executors, shuffles or AQE; streams run only as availableNow here
gaps.closes_with: File layout lessons locally; Spark tuning verified in Fabric

gaps.title: Monitoring hub, alerts, refresh
gaps.closes_with: Recorded run histories (SIMULATED), live read-only checks later

gaps.title: Item behavior only the service shows
gaps.why: Workspace Git sync, deployment, triggers, shortcuts, copy throughput and V-Order happen in Fabric; locally the learner works with the files and the logic

gaps.title: No local Power Query (M) engine
gaps.why: orchestration/mashup.py reads dataflow definitions but nothing evaluates M
gaps.closes_with: SIMULATED fault diagnosis locally; Fabric exercise (ACD-014)
